text.p: Campbell Soup Co is reviewing operations generating $1.4 billion in yearly sales as part of a strategy to focus the company's holdings on core businesses, but the company has made no decisions on whether to sell any or all of the units, spokesman Leonard Griehs said Monday.
He said analysts were informed of the review at a meeting Friday.

The $1.4 billion figure refers to units that have neither been identified as core businesses, generating $6.1 billion in sales, nor as operations generating $500 million in revenues that have already been targeted for a selloff, Griehs said.
"There is an additional $1.4 billion in sales that we're generating that we would consider as less-strategic businesses, or non-strategic businesses," he said.
"We're evaluating currently what's the best strategy to create the most wealth for our shareowners from the current portfolio of business that we have," he said.
Campbell's core businesses are, soups, sauces, bakery and biscuits, and foodservice, he said.

He declined to identify businesses being reviewed. Analysts have speculated, after Friday's meeting and previously, that Campbell may sell its Swanson frozen foods and Vlasic pickles lines, among others.

Nesbitt Burns food analyst Ellen Baras said Swanson's would be a more likely target than market-leader Vlasic. She said outside of food-giant ConAgra Inc, there are few obvious potential buyers, but a small buyout group such as one led by managers could also be a purchaser.
Griehs said Campbell has not discussed a timetable for the evaluation. "We'll provide further updates in the near-term," he said.
Campbell has been selling off non-core assets over the last several years.
In announcing a restructuring and stock buyback last September, the company said it would sell several businesses, with sales of about $500 million, over a two-year period.
The company said in May it had sold its "Marie's" salad dressing line and its poultry operations.
